text: 1. Conserve coolant at every junction
textPreview: 1. Conserve coolant at every junction

text: Σ ṁin = Σ ṁout        and        Σ ṁi = ṁrack
textPreview: Σ ṁin = Σ ṁout        and        Σ ṁi = ṁrack

text: 2. Allocate flow according to heat
textPreview: 2. Allocate flow according to heat

text: ṁi* = ṁrack × Q̇i / Σ Q̇i
textPreview: ṁi* = ṁrack × Q̇i / Σ Q̇i

text: At 120 L/min: compute target = 6.02 L/min per tray; switch = 1.29 L/min.
textPreview: At 120 L/min: compute target = 6.02 L/min per tray; switch = 1.29 L/min.

text: 3. Solve each tray energy balance
textPreview: 3. Solve each tray energy balance

text: Q̇i = ṁi [h(Tout,i) − h(Tin)]        h(T) = ∫ cp(T) dT
textPreview: Q̇i = ṁi [h(Tout,i) − h(Tin)]        h(T) = ∫ cp(T) dT

text: Flow error (%) = 100 √{(1/n) Σ [(ṁi / ṁi*) − 1]²}
textPreview: Flow error (%) = 100 √{(1/n) Σ [(ṁi / ṁi*) − 1]²}

text:
Notation: ṁ = mass flow (kg/s), Q̇ = thermal power (W), V̇ = volume flow (m³/s), h = specific enthalpy (J/kg), cp = specific heat (J/kg/K). Common inlet state makes inlet-reference volume targets proportional to heat. Exact thermal calculation integrates the tabulated cp(T).

textPreview: Kh = [√(1 − β⁴(1 − Cd²)) − Cd β²]² |                  / (2ρ Cd² Ao²)

text: For required Kh, invert this relation to obtain bore d. Smaller bores increase resistance.
textPreview: For required Kh, invert this relation to obtain bore d. Smaller bores increase resistance.

text: 0 < d < D; Cd = 0.62 is assumed.
textPreview: 0 < d < D; Cd = 0.62 is assumed.

alt: Penn shield watermark from supplied template

text:
Equations implemented in components.py and orifices.py. Kh has units Pa/(kg/s)^2 and differs from dimensionless minor-loss K. Cd = 0.62 is a screening assumption for a thin, sharp-edged plate. The permanent-loss relation accounts for recovery; pressure-tap differential alone is not permanent loss. Header model omits 3D tee momentum recovery.

text: [7]  Sources and calculation details in speaker notes.

text: Pump operating point and electrical power
textPreview: Pump operating point and electrical power

text: Δppump = Δp0 N² − aV̇² = Δpsystem        Pe = Δp V̇ / η
textPreview: Δppump = Δp0 N² − aV̇² = Δpsystem        Pe = Δp V̇ / η

text: Fixed-flow mode evaluates the head required. Pump mode solves the curve intersection.
textPreview: Fixed-flow mode evaluates the head required. Pump mode solves the curve intersection.

text: Facility water removes the rack heat
textPreview: Facility water removes the rack heat

text: Q̇HX = Σ Q̇i = ṁFWS [h(TFWS,out) − h(TFWS,in)]
textPreview: Q̇HX = Σ Q̇i = ṁFWS [h(TFWS,out) − h(TFWS,in)]

text: Heat-exchanger conductance required
textPreview: Heat-exchanger conductance required

text: UArequired = Q̇HX / ΔTlm        ΔTlm = (ΔT1 − ΔT2) / ln(ΔT1/ΔT2)
textPreview: UArequired = Q̇HX / ΔTlm        ΔTlm = (ΔT1 − ΔT2) / ln(ΔT1/ΔT2)

alt: Penn shield watermark from supplied template

text:
Pump curve uses an assumed parabolic shape fitted to a nominal point and assumed shutoff head. It is not a measured manufacturer curve. Pinches: ΔT1 = rack return minus facility return; ΔT2 = rack supply minus facility supply. Both must be positive. Equal terminal differences use the continuous LMTD limit. No ambient heat loss or pump heat is included in the quoted rack balance.
